New Mexico context: the east of the state (Lea, Eddy, Chaves, Roosevelt and Curry counties) is in the Southwest Power Pool and served by Xcel's Southwestern Public Service (SPS). Since the 2026 western expansion the SPP queue also holds Farmington Electric's requests. The rest of the state has no market: PNM, El Paso Electric, Tri-State, Farmington and Los Alamos County each run their own interconnection. The New Mexico Public Regulation Commission regulates PNM, SPS and El Paso Electric; its docket system is PRCe360, and the harvest of its cases is under batches/us-nm/harvest/. Air permits come from three agencies: the New Mexico Environment Department Air Quality Bureau for most of the state (its APMAP record, harvested into scopes/us-nm/work/permits/), the City of Albuquerque Air Quality Program for Bernalillo County (Reeves, Rio Bravo), and EPA Region 9 for the Navajo Nation (NTEC). Local planning records are in batches/us-nm/harvest/local_records.md.
